text: Eleanor's Pot Roast is the best thing in Astoria. Grandmother's recipe, you can taste the love. The Eleanor cocktail pairs perfectly.
Our anniversary table every month. Carlton always remembers us. The Grilled NY Strip was cooked exactly to temp.
Daniel in the kitchen is a genius. The Charred Octopus and Clay-Pot Chicken were unreal. Wonderful American wine list.
Great neighborhood tavern. Tavern Burger is solid, Brussels sprouts addictive. Got a touch loud on a Saturday but that's the vibe.
The new winter menu made our week. Deviled eggs, clam chowder, and a bourbon flight. Astoria gem.
Took the family for Sarah's birthday. Apple pie a la mode and the staff sang. Sophia runs a tight, warm room.
Food is genuinely good but we waited 40 minutes past our reservation on a Friday. Pot roast made up for it, mostly.
Shepherd's Pie and the soft pretzel are comfort food perfection. American wines by the glass are well chosen.
Reliable, hearty, and the Meatloaf is a sleeper hit. Bourbon Pecan Pie is dangerous. Service a bit slow when packed.
Grilled Atlantic Salmon was perfect and the Maple Roasted Carrots were a surprise standout. Fish is always fresh here.
Off night for us. Pan-Seared Cod came out lukewarm and the table was sticky. Manager comped dessert, appreciated that.
Best tavern in Queens, full stop. The Eleanor cocktail, Fish & Chips, and that fireplace in winter. We're regulars now.
Hosted a private dinner upstairs. Carlton and Sophia handled 22 of us flawlessly. Steak Sandwich for the table was a hit.
Cozy and consistent. Mac & Cheese and Garlic Mashed are great sides. Wish they had more vegetarian mains.
Holiday hours dinner was magical. Seasonal Cobbler and a glass of American red. Felt like family.
Tavern Wings and a craft beer at the bar with Nina pouring. My after-work spot for years.
Solid Sunday dinner. Pot Roast as good as everyone says. Loud kids' table near us but staff was gracious.
The fall menu rollout nailed it. Clay-Pot Chicken and a bourbon flight. Daniel keeps getting better.
Astoria institution. The portions are massive and the staff treat you like family.
Great spot for a cold-weather afternoon pint. Goes way back, a true Astoria classic.
Good brisket and a fun bar. Gets crowded on weekends but worth it.
Lovely wine bar with a thoughtful list. Great for a quiet date night in the neighborhood.
Charming little French spot. Reservations a must, tiny room. Lovely cassoulet.
